title: Rose clay and rose geranium cold-process soap
subtitle: A soft pink conditioning bar with a floral scent
excerpt: A cold-process bar built on olive, coconut, and shea butter, with rose kaolin clay giving a dusty pink tone and rose geranium essential oil for a warm floral scent. Makes 7 bars; ready after a 4 to 6 week maturation.
sourceNotes: Rose kaolin clay in cold-process soap: general soapmaking reference. Rose geranium essential oil (Pelargonium roseum) stability in alkaline soap batter: general aromatherapy and soapmaking reference. Floral essential oils tend to fade in CP soap; using 3 to 4% of oil weight retains some scent in the cured bar. SAP values from SoapCalc.

recipe.batchNotes: Run any scale change through a lye calculator.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Two years in a cool dark cupboard once cured. The rose geranium scent fades somewhat in the alkaline bar; what remains is a soft floral background. Discard if DOS or a rancid smell develop.

glossaryTerms.definition: The reaction between fat and sodium hydroxide that produces soap and glycerine. Each oil has a SAP value: grams of lye per gram of oil.
The percentage of oil left unsaponified in the finished bar, typically 5%. At 5% superfat, the bar is mild and conditioning.
The point at which soap batter thickens to thin-custard consistency. A drizzle on the surface briefly holds its shape.

projectSchedule.title: Unmould and cut
projectSchedule.body: Turn out the loaf. The bar will be a warm dusty pink from the rose clay. Cut wearing protective gloves.

projectSchedule.title: Turn the bars
projectSchedule.body: Flip each bar. The pink tone may lighten slightly as the bar loses moisture and firms up.

projectSchedule.title: Four-week test
projectSchedule.body: Press a sliver to the tongue. No sting means safe to use. A light floral scent should persist.

projectSchedule.title: Cure complete
projectSchedule.body: A fully cured bar is firm, pink-toned, and produces a creamy lather. Store on an open rack.

content.text: A conditioning cold-process bar coloured with rose kaolin clay and scented with rose geranium essential oil. Rose clay gives the bar a natural dusty-pink tone without synthetic colourant. The 5%
superfat
and the shea butter base make it mild and suitable for dry skin. Floral essential oils fade in the alkaline
saponification
process; a 3% loading by oil weight is needed to retain a noticeable scent in the cured bar.
Put on protective gloves and goggles before handling lye.
Ingredients

items.prepNote: calculated at 5% superfat for this oil blend
3% of oil weight; dispersed in a tablespoon of oil before adding to batter
3% of oil weight; add at trace; use a light trace as rose geranium can accelerate

content.text: Method
Mix lye solution
In a ventilated space with protective gloves and goggles on, add the sodium hydroxide to the distilled water in a steady stream. Stir until dissolved. Cool to 38 to 42°C.
Prepare oils and disperse clay
Melt coconut oil and shea butter. Add olive oil and castor oil. Cool to 38 to 42°C. Disperse the rose kaolin clay in two tablespoons of the oil blend to form a smooth paste.
Blend to trace and add clay and fragrance
Pour the lye solution into the oils. Blend to light
trace
. Add the rose geranium essential oil and the clay paste. Stir by hand to incorporate. Pour immediately as rose geranium can accelerate the batter.
Insulate, unmould, and cure
Wrap in a towel. Leave 48 hours. Unmould wearing protective gloves. Cut into bars. Cure 4 to 6 weeks on a rack.
Storage and shelf life
Two years in a cool dark cupboard. The pink tone and the floral scent both lighten slightly over time.
